This isn't enough information to help, unfortunately. I tried exporting with shader baker on 4.5.1 with the Platformer 3D Demo and couldn't reproduce the problem.

Does this occur on a demo project like that on your system? If not, trying to pare down your project into a smaller, shareable version that still produces the crash would be the best bet. If that's not possible, building Godot from source yourself would at least allow you to post the stacktrace.

Please do also include all of the system information from Help > Copy System Info, that doesn't seem like all of the information it should give.

There are two potential factors involved here:
1. There is known issue with the shader baker when trying to export shaders with errors in them. This was fixed in 4.6 with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112803
2. Its unclear if you are using the Compatibility renderer or the Forward+ renderer. The Shader Baker is not supported in the Compatibility renderer (it shouldn't crash though)

> 
>     2. Its unclear if you are using the Compatibility renderer or the Forward+ renderer. The Shader Baker is not supported in the Compatibility renderer (it shouldn't crash though)

Using forward+

Was hitting this issue too. Not sure if it's the same or unrelated but posting to help anyone else out. The shader baker seems to enable some code that wants to traverse all export vars. I guess this is how export plugins search for what needs handling by them. The problem however, is If you have an export var with a cyclic reference, it gets stuck in a loop. See the stack trace. My fix was not to use a cyclic reference.
